full_judgment:
7. After coming to know about the cancellation of the lease the petitioner filed a representation to the Government on 21.6.79 with a prayer to re-vise the cancellation order. On receipt of the above representation the Government issued a notice on 4.7.79 upon the petitioner to produce all his relevant documents and also to hear him at the office of the relevant officer of the Government. Accordingly, the petitioner appeared before the relevant officer and produced all the documents in support of his representation. Thereafter the petitioner also sent several letters to the relevant officers of the Government for considering the matter but it appears that the Government sat over the matter for about 6 (six) years without giving any reply to the representations. Ultimately, on 7.2.85 the Government passed the impugned order (Annexure CC) intimating that for violation of the terms of the lease deed the Government has cancelled the lease and the Government had decided to sell this land like other lands in open auction. For that reason it was not possible for the Government to reconsider the order of cancellation of lease passed earlier. 

 15. Again the Government without delivering the total area of the demised land to the petitioner or giving any reply whatsoever of so many letters and representations of the petitioner, issued another show cause notice for the second time on 29.1.71 stating that since the petitioner violated the condition No. 3 of the indenture, why his lease should not be terminated. The self-same ground as given in the previous notice was also given in the second show cause notice. On receipt of the show cause notice for the second time the petitioner had given a detailed reply on 9.2.71 describing the short delivery of demised land and mentioning about the representations made earlier to the authorities concerned. On receipt of the above reply the Government sat over the matter indefinitely without giving the petitioner any reply. On 25.1.71 the petitioner paid instalment as required for the demised land. Then the petitioner sought per-mission from the then Dhaka Improvement Trust now Rajuk for construction of the building on the demised plot. D.I.T. asked the petitioner to have clearance from the concerned Ministry and in pursuance of that letter the petitioner applied to the Government in 1977 and 1978 on several occasions praying for relevant clearance but the Government remained silent over the matter. For that reason the plan submitted by the petitioner to D.I.T. could not be passed.
